name: Richard Nixon
description: US president associated with détente, Vietnamisation, domestic regulation and Watergate.
scope: Public positions and conduct during the specified period; this represents the individual rather than all party members or citizens.

axes.brief: Nixon competed in elections but Watergate conduct undermined accountability.
axes.counter: Resignation and compliance with the tapes ruling show limits to presidential authority.

axes.brief: Law-and-order policy, the drug war and secret surveillance expanded state coercion.
axes.counter: Constitutional speech and judicial limits persisted despite abusive conduct.

axes.brief: Shared national identity coexisted with school integration and minority-business support.
axes.counter: Southern electoral strategy and private prejudice complicate equal-cultural recognition.

axes.brief: Immigration was managed within the existing legal framework rather than abolished.
axes.counter: This is less directly evidenced than defence or economic policy; exact admissions mechanisms are estimates.

axes.brief: Bombing and military threats coexisted with troop withdrawals and negotiated arms limits.
axes.counter: Détente and ending conscription limit unqualified militarism.

axes.brief: National-interest diplomacy retained US sovereignty within longstanding alliances.
axes.counter: International agreements did constrain some arms and trade policy.

axes.brief: Private enterprise remained the norm; government established Amtrak and maintained public functions.
axes.counter: Government creation of selected enterprises differs from broad nationalisation.

axes.brief: The 1971 import surcharge coexisted with subsequent negotiation and openness.
axes.counter: The temporary surcharge is not evidence for permanent blanket tariffs.

axes.brief: Price controls and federal regulation operated inside a private market economy.
axes.counter: Emergency controls differed from permanent comprehensive production planning.

axes.brief: He proposed a basic family-income floor and expanded benefits while stressing work.
axes.counter: The Family Assistance Plan failed; it is a proposal rather than implemented entitlement.

axes.brief: Civil government coexisted with public religion and support for religious schooling.
axes.counter: Religious rhetoric does not establish clerical vetoes over civil law.

axes.brief: Conventional family norms and resistance to counterculture shaped social policy.
axes.counter: School integration and female appointments prevent equating every reform with rejection.

axes.brief: Environmental regulation and EPA creation coexisted with technology and growth.
axes.counter: Environmental institution-building does not prove positions on modern enhancement.

axes.brief: New Federalism favoured revenue sharing and local discretion.
axes.counter: Foreign policy and several regulatory institutions remained centrally controlled.

axes.brief: Merit and family explanations coexisted with structural and discriminatory accounts.
axes.counter: Private racial stereotypes are not a documented position on each genetics claim.
axes.gap: The behavioural-causation items are tentative estimates; rhetoric, prejudice and moral traditionalism must not substitute for a specific biological claim.

sources.title: Richard Nixon — biographical and policy overview
